title: Session fingerprinting + phased backoff defaults and scoped idempotency guidance for SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers experience noisy duplicate requests, uneven retry costs, and poor UX when streamed responses are interrupted. Current SDK defaults are conservative but inconsistent across languages, and streaming resume semantics vary. Goal: Define a cross-SDK approach that (1) phases retry/backoff defaults by call pattern and latency tier, (2) introduces a lightweight session fingerprinting model to bound dedup windows, and (3) scopes idempotency key recommendations for non-idempotent endpoints and streaming checkpoints. Deliverables: - Definitive default backoff profile per SDK (fast/normal/conservative) mapped to latency tiers and request cost budget. - Session fingerprint spec (opaque client-generated token + server-side soft dedup window) with rotation guidance. - Scoped idempotency key cookbook: when to auto-generate, when to require user-supplied keys, naming/scoping conventions, and recommended TTLs. - Streaming resume token format and migration path for existing stream clients. - Examples in Python, TypeScript, Go showing best practices and minimal ergonomic primitives (helpers that auto-generate idemp keys, attach session fingerprints, and persist resume tokens). Constraints & trade-offs: - Keep surface area small: prefer helper functions over complex new APIs to avoid breaking changes. - Server-side dedup window must be conservative to avoid hiding real retries; recommend 5s for short-lived non-chunked calls, 60s for sessioned streaming in default config, configurable via SDK/request options. - Avoid storing long-lived secrets in idempotency keys. Use opaque base64 and optional HMAC prefix for tenants who require stronger anti-forgery. - Telemetry: emit retry_reason, retry_phase, session_fingerprint, idemp_source (auto|user) to help ops tune budgets. Acceptance criteria: - Design doc reviewed by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and Security/Privacy. - Implementation PRs with unit tests and e2e retry simulations for each SDK. - Console telemetry dashboards created for retry budget exhaustion and dedup-positive events. - Migration guidance published in SDK docs and a short changelog entry.

examples:
Python (recommended helper)

from redwood_sdk import Client, generate_idempotency, session_fingerprint
client = Client(api_key=... )

idemp = generate_idempotency(prefix='billing')
sf = session_fingerprint()
resp = client.create_invoice(amount=1200, idempotency_key=idemp, headers={'X-RW-Session': sf})

TypeScript (minimal helper)

import {Client, genIdemp, sessionFingerprint} from 'redwood-sdk'
const client = new Client({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY})
const idemp = genIdemp('billing')
const sf = sessionFingerprint()
await client.createInvoice({amount: 1200}, {idempotencyKey: idemp, headers: { 'X-RW-Session': sf }})

Go (pattern)

idemp := redwood.GenIdemp("billing")
sf := redwood.SessionFingerprint()
resp, err := client.CreateInvoice(context.Background(), &CreateInvoiceParams{Amount:1200}, WithIdempotency(idemp), WithHeader("X-RW-Session", sf))
notes:
Phased backoff proposal: - Fast: initial_delay=50ms, multiplier=1.8, max_delay=500ms, attempts=3. Use for idempotent/low-cost calls (embeddings). - Normal: initial_delay=150ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=2s, attempts=4. Use for generation requests with short sequences. - Conservative: initial_delay=300ms, multiplier=2.2, max_delay=8s, attempts=6. Use for customer-facing long-running ops (model fine-tunes, admin calls).

Session fingerprinting: - Client generates opaque 12-byte random token, base64-url encoded. - Attach in header X-RW-Session. - Server keeps soft dedup map for token+endpoint with TTL based on call class (see defaults above). - SDKs rotate session fingerprint on process restart and expose manual rotate() to apps that want shorter windows.

Scoped idempotency: - Auto-generate idemp keys for high-throughput clients when safe (stateless idemp e.g., billing charge attempt). - For multi-step workflows, recommend user-provided keys with scope: tenant:workflow:action:uuid. - TTL: default 24h for billing-like ops, 7d for long-lived resource creation only if server retention supported.

Streaming resume token: - Server returns Resume-Token header (opaque). SDK persists named tokens by stream_id. - Resume token format: base64 of (stream_id || seq_offset || HMAC(optional)). - On reconnect SDK attempts resume; if server rejects token, SDK falls back to restart-with-cooldown and emits telemetry event 'stream_resume_failed'.

Telemetry & observability: emit structured fields: retry_reason (network, server-5xx, rate-limit), retry_phase (fast|normal|conservative), session_fingerprint, idemp_source (auto|user), resume_attempted (true|false), resume_success (true|false).
